reader.requirement: At --std 85, after a REWRITE of an indexed file control must follow IX.1.3.5: an invalid key condition (21, 22, 23) with INVALID KEY runs that imperative (no USE procedure, NOT INVALID KEY ignored, a GO TO transfers); without INVALID KEY the file's USE procedure runs; a non-invalid-key exception (43, 44, 49) runs the USE procedure and neither phrase; success runs NOT INVALID KEY, else continues after the statement.

edition-consulted.switches: InForce (edition year < 2002): at 85 a REWRITE of an indexed file with neither INVALID KEY nor an applicable USE procedure is refused (COBOL6826, IX.4.6.3 SR3), so the 'neither' control path cannot arise at 85; from 2002 it compiles

reader.edition-search: grep 'Edition|CobolVersion|DialectBehavior|IsAtLeast' over KeyedIoEmitter.cs, SequentialIoEmitter.cs, IoStatusClass.cs, KeyedIoBinder.cs and ExceptionPhraseRequirement.cs: the run-time phrase branches (EmitInvalid/EmitPhrasePair) read no edition; the one edition read on the REWRITE path is the compile-time SR3 requirement in ExceptionPhraseRequirement.Require.
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: yes: at 85 the form with neither INVALID KEY nor a USE procedure is refused at compile time (SR3); at 2023 it compiles and runs (status 23, no phrase). The transfer of control for every form 85 admits is the same code
reader.witnesses-cover: part: l1c26_rewrite_relative_invalid_key is a RELATIVE file; the indexed REWRITE (the module of this rule), the USE path when INVALID KEY is absent, non-invalid-key exceptions (43, 49), the 21 and 22 invalid keys and a GO TO out of the INVALID KEY phrase are not in it.

probes.printed: T1 INVALID 23 (no USE, no NOT-INVALID); T2 NOT-INVALID 00; T3 USE-IX 22 (NOT INVALID ignored); T4 after 00; T5 AT M2 23 (GO TO); T6 USE-IX 49 (no phrase); T7 USE-IQ 43 (sequential, no prior READ; no phrase); T8 INVALID 21 (sequential, prime key changed); T9 NOT-INVALID 00
probes.expected: IX.1.3.5 items (2)/(3) for the invalid key condition, items (1)/(2) of its second list for exceptions that are not invalid key and for success, over random/dynamic and sequential access

probes.printed: T4: a REWRITE with neither phrase, successful: continues, 00
probes.expected: the degenerate form: no phrase, control passes to the next statement
IX.4.6.3 SR3 requires INVALID KEY when no applicable USE procedure exists, so 85 refuses the form a later edition admits

OK  §1985:IX.1.3.5  (1.3.5 The Invalid Key Condition)  the text is in the clause; it lies in GR2
OK  §1985:IX.1.3.5  (1.3.5 The Invalid Key Condition)  the text is in the clause; it lies in GRL2.1

reader.notes: The keyed REWRITE stores the status, runs the USE hook (marked as handled when INVALID KEY is written), then renders the INVALID/NOT INVALID pair on the 2x and 0x status classes through the one EmitPhrasePair. All nine probed control paths match IX.1.3.5.

refuter.evidence: E:/COBOL-coord/scratch/coderead-1985/out/refute-1985-008/c/rw02.cob at --std 85 (random access, USE procedure present): a REWRITE that creates an allowed alternate duplicate gives 02 and runs NOT INVALID KEY with no USE (successful completion, IX.1.3.5 second list item 2); the same without an INVALID KEY phrase runs NOT INVALID KEY; a duplicate on a unique alternate key without INVALID KEY runs the USE procedure (22) and not NOT INVALID KEY. Later-edition REWRITE phrases refused (E:/COBOL-coord/scratch/coderead-1985/out/refute-1985-008/f/l1-l3,l11: FILE phrase, lock phrases, RETRY, FROM literal). cite.py: 'OK  §1985:IX.4.6.4 GR10  (4.6.4 General Rules)  the text is in GR10'; 'OK  §1985:IX.1.3.5  (1.3.5 The Invalid Key Condition)  the text is in the clause; it lies in GRL2.2'. Side note (not this rule): a REWRITE leaving an already-duplicated AK unchanged answers 00, a reading of 'created a duplicate' in IX.1.3.4 1b2 that GR10's control transfer does not depend on.
